cues.text: East of the birches the trail dips, and between the pines there is firelight. Goblin voices, arguing about something.

cues.speaker: brannoc
cues.text: Three voices. A fire. They're not expecting anyone.

cues.speaker: ilsevel
cues.text: I should say, before anyone is brave, that I have nothing left but cantrips. And I am bleeding. A little.

cues.speaker: oriel
cues.text: I've used every prayer I had tonight. Until I sleep, I've only the small ones.

cues.speaker: brannoc
cues.text: Then we wait for dawn.

cues.speaker: tamsin
cues.text: By dawn that cart's gone, Big Man. Wherever it's going.

cues.speaker: tamsin
cues.text: Rusk told us what goblins like to hear. Stones, a boss, supper. Let me walk in there and tell them a story.

cues.speaker: brannoc
cues.text: Alone.

cues.speaker: tamsin
cues.text: Alone's the only way anyone believes a story. You lot creep up to the bushes and look large.

cues.speaker: oriel
cues.text: And if it goes wrong?

cues.speaker: tamsin
cues.text: Then come and save me. Heroically. I'll scream, so you know when.
They go in through the undergrowth, one careful step at a time.
Brannoc's mail whispers at every step and Ilsevel walks face-first into a branch. But Tamsin picks the path, Oriel steadies the rest, and nobody hears them.
Three goblins around a fire, a patched tent, and a cart with something grey in its straw. Tamsin walks into the light as if she owns the woods.

cues.speaker: tamsin
cues.text: Evening, lads! Boss sent me. Change of plan: the stones go tonight. And where's my supper?
The lie is so cheerful, and so sure of itself, that the goblins simply swallow it. Two of them even step away from their knives.

cues.speaker: goblin-1
cues.text: Tonight? Cart goes at dawn. Always dawn. Boss counts every stone, he does.

cues.speaker: tamsin
cues.text: And now he wants them early. Lovely fire, by the way.
Behind the goblins, a grey shield rises slowly out of the bushes.

cues.speaker: goblin-2
cues.text: Why boss send a dwarf?

cues.speaker: tamsin
cues.text: Ah. That'll be my cue.

battle_narration.text: Tamsin has an arrow on the string before the goblins have finished turning round.
Brannoc comes out of the bushes at a run and does not stop until the first runt is down.
The leader's blade catches Tamsin across the arm. She staggers, white-faced.
Tamsin bites the stopper out of a little red bottle and drinks it in one swallow.
Brannoc's sword finds the goblin leader. He does not get up.
Golden fire drops out of the dark onto the last runt, and the camp is theirs.

cues.speaker: oriel
cues.text: Tamsin! Your arm...

cues.speaker: tamsin
cues.text: Potion. Always carry one. Old habit.

cues.speaker: brannoc
cues.text: That was a good lie.

cues.speaker: tamsin
cues.text: It was, wasn't it? I'm a little bit proud of it, Big Man.
In the cart's straw lie three lantern-cores. They should glow like small suns. They are cloudy, and cold as river stones.

cues.speaker: ilsevel
cues.text: Three. Three lanterns somewhere along this road are dark tonight, and nobody has written it down.

cues.speaker: ilsevel
cues.text: A core is always warm. This is like holding a stone from the bottom of a well.

cues.speaker: oriel
cues.text: I can't touch them. I'm sorry. I don't know why.

cues.speaker: tamsin
cues.text: Which one's Thirty-Seven, Professor?

cues.speaker: ilsevel
cues.text: I do not know. Nobody numbers the cores. Perhaps somebody should have.

cues.speaker: brannoc
cues.text: We take all three. Then we find somewhere to sleep that isn't here.

cues.speaker: ilsevel
cues.text: Pell says there is a hollow south of the fork. Sheltered. There is an old stone in it.

cues.speaker: brannoc
cues.text: Then we sleep there. I'll take first watch.

next_time: A campfire, a long watch, and an old stone.
